findings.title: Make revision-fenced saves an actual cross-process transaction
findings.actual: Two concurrent requests could read the same base digest, both report success, and let the later replace silently erase the earlier save.
findings.expected: Each canonical board path has one cross-process mutation lane; a same-base race produces exactly one winner and one explicit conflict.
findings.reproduce: Queue two same-base saves behind one held path lock, then release both together.
findings.proof: Deterministic Python concurrency coverage asserts one success, one WorkspaceConflictError, and disk bytes equal to the winning response.
findings.seam: workspace_store.py + server.py; stdlib advisory locks live under the shared release home, never beside user boards.
findings.acceptance: Concurrent save/save, save/rename, and save/trash outcomes are equivalent to a valid sequential order; directories are fsynced after replacement.

findings.title: Make portable export non-destructive and no-clobber by default
findings.actual: File → Export detached the live editor, awaited disk I/O, bailed history afterward, cleared dirty state, and forced replacement of an existing .tldr.
findings.expected: Export snapshots into the existing hidden clone and requires a second explicit Replace choice when the destination exists.
findings.reproduce: Export an authored board and compare the live editor snapshot and source-file bytes before and after; separately export onto an existing distinctive .tldr.
findings.proof: The portable-clone browser smoke proves the live snapshot stays byte-identical; the File-export smoke proves the source file stays intact and an occupied target stays byte-exact until explicit Replace.
findings.seam: LocalWorkspace delegates to portableTldraw.ts and reuses the Save As conflict state.
findings.acceptance: Export leaves the live editor snapshot and source file unchanged, and it cannot alter an existing target until the user chooses Replace.

findings.title: Fence automatic reloads against edits made while the read is in flight
findings.actual: The watcher decided to reload while clean, awaited a GET, then applied it and marked clean even if the user edited during that wait.
findings.expected: Automatic reload captures the local epoch and base revision, then rechecks them immediately before replacing editor state.
findings.reproduce: Delay the GET after an external rewrite is observed, make a real canvas edit, then release the GET.
findings.proof: A focused fence regression enumerates edit-epoch, base-digest, and loaded-digest changes that must refuse the apply; the full workspace browser journeys remain green.
findings.seam: LocalWorkspace automatic reload only; explicit Use disk version remains the intentional discard path.
findings.acceptance: No automatic read may erase an edit or clear dirty state that appeared after the read began.

findings.title: Use content digests for external-change decisions
findings.actual: Polling compared only size and floating-point mtime, so a same-size rewrite with a restored/coarse timestamp could remain invisible.
findings.expected: The stat contract carries a bounded SHA-256 over the exact raw file bytes, matching the revision identity used by writes and conflicts.
findings.reproduce: Rewrite a board with different same-length bytes and restore its original mtime.
findings.proof: Python tests hash raw bytes before text decoding and enforce the document-size bound; Python and TypeScript regressions assert the fingerprint changes even when size and mtime do not.
findings.seam: workspace_store.stat_document → workspace stat API → workspaceModel DocumentFingerprint.
findings.acceptance: A same-size, same-mtime external rewrite triggers reload when clean and conflict when locally dirty.

findings.title: Bound workspace requests and keep external polling single-flight
findings.actual: Raw fetch calls could wait forever, and the 1.5-second watcher could stack another stat request behind every stalled predecessor.
findings.expected: Operations have explicit deadlines/cancellation semantics and at most one external-stat poll is active.
findings.reproduce: Accept a request but never answer it, then let several poll intervals elapse.
findings.proof: Controlled-fetch tests prove timeout classification and caller abort propagation; the watch loop has an explicit in-flight guard and abortable request, backed by zero-error workspace browser journeys.
findings.seam: workspaceClient request helper plus LocalWorkspace watch effect; any automatic retry remains digest-fenced, so an uncertain prior success becomes a conflict rather than a double-write.
findings.acceptance: A stalled controller resolves to actionable UI inside its budget, cleanup aborts stale reads, and request count stays bounded.

findings.title: Retry transient autosave failures without waiting for another edit
findings.actual: After one transient write failure the board stayed dirty indefinitely unless the user edited again or manually saved.
findings.expected: Autosave retries with bounded backoff, resets after success, and never loops on a real revision conflict.
findings.reproduce: Make the first autosave fail transiently and let the next attempt succeed without another canvas mutation.
findings.proof: Model tests freeze the 1s/3s/8s retry schedule and stop conditions; client tests limit retries to transport, timeout, 408, 429, and 5xx failures.
findings.seam: LocalWorkspace autosave scheduler; the digest fence remains authoritative.
findings.acceptance: Transient failure self-heals; retry stops on success, conflict, unmount, or document switch.

findings.title: Turn workspace failures into recoverable, named actions
findings.actual: Several File-menu promises were discarded, while an initial list/read error stranded the app on a message with no Retry.
findings.expected: One action boundary surfaces the failed operation, and bootstrap can retry without restarting the app.
findings.reproduce: Reject New, Open, Reveal, or Trash; separately fail the first startup request and succeed the second.
findings.proof: The central action runner contains every launched promise, bootstrap renders an explicit Try again path, and all normal workspace browser journeys finish with zero console errors.
findings.seam: LocalWorkspace action runner + WorkspaceLoading recovery controls.
findings.acceptance: Every launched action completes or presents a visible recovery path; successful Retry reaches the canvas.

findings.title: Make the workspace browser a real keyboard modal
findings.actual: Physical Tab escaped the Open dialog after its last control and continued into the canvas toolbar.
findings.expected: Useful initial focus enters the dialog, Tab and Shift+Tab loop inside, Escape closes only it, and focus returns to its launcher.
findings.reproduce: Open with Ctrl+O, traverse past both ends using physical keys, then press Escape.
findings.proof: A focus-order regression and real in-app browser journey record each active element and return focus.
findings.seam: WorkspaceDialog DOM behavior only; stock canvas keyboard handling is unchanged.
findings.acceptance: Focus never leaves the modal while open and close restores the element that launched it.

findings.title: Make Block creation and section resizing operable from the keyboard
findings.actual: Add Port was a div with role=button and tabIndex=-1; Expanded section dividers supported pointer drags only.
findings.expected: Add Port is a native focused action, while each divider exposes separator value semantics and arrow-key resizing.
findings.reproduce: Select an Expanded Block, Tab to a port bead, press Enter/Space, then adjust dividers with arrows and a coarse modifier.
findings.proof: Markup/math regressions prove native semantics, clamping, and the shared pointer equation; the permanent CDP smoke proves real Tab/Space/Enter/ArrowDown, while the driven review fixture recorded divider values 40 → 42 → 35 → 42 → 40 through adjustment and Undo.
findings.seam: BlockCanvas native DOM semantics around the existing Block seam; tldraw drag/resize stays stock.
findings.acceptance: Add Port is focusable and keyboard-activatable; dividers announce their values, use the shared resize updater, clamp correctly, and each keyboard adjustment remains undoable.

findings.title: Keep transient chrome usable on narrow canvases
findings.actual: At 560 px the selection pill measured 569 px and extended 29 px offscreen; Shapes and Inspector overlapped almost entirely.
findings.expected: The pill stays inside the 20 px safe area with keyboard-reachable overflow, while an interface-scale-aware compact breakpoint keeps only the newest side panel visible.
findings.reproduce: At 560 px and default Interface size, then at 900 px and 160%, open a wide generic selection menu and open Shapes followed by Inspector or Comments.
findings.proof: Pure placement/state coverage plus real-browser rectangles prove no horizontal overflow or panel overlap, including compact behavior adjusted for enlarged Interface size.
findings.seam: Selection menu CSS/placement and ChromeProvider responsive state; desktop coexistence is preserved.
findings.acceptance: At the tested compact widths and Interface sizes every action stays reachable, and opening one compact side sheet closes the other.

findings.title: Make immediate close durable for boards above the browser keepalive budget
findings.actual: The final pagehide path sends the whole document with keepalive; realistic review boards already exceed the practical queued-body ceiling.
findings.expected: A host-owned checkpoint/ack protocol persists the last edit regardless of size.
findings.reproduce: Edit a large board and immediately close the app.
findings.proof: Architecture audit measured an existing board above the practical limit.
findings.acceptance: Cold reopen contains the exact final edit after repeated immediate closes.

findings.title: Replace Obsidian's fixed close delay with checkpoint acknowledgement
findings.actual: The host sleeps 450 ms and unmounts while it ignores checkpoint messages already emitted by the canvas.
findings.expected: Persist or acknowledge the final opaque snapshot before teardown.
findings.reproduce: Delay serialization beyond 450 ms, edit, close, and reopen.
findings.proof: VS Code already implements this protocol.
findings.acceptance: The delayed final edit reopens exactly without a timing guess.

findings.title: Quarantine schema-invalid embedded documents before host writeback
findings.actual: Embedded parse failure can remain editable and post a blank fallback snapshot.
findings.expected: All hosts share one quarantined load decision and suppress writes.
findings.reproduce: Open invalid bytes in a packaged host and attempt an edit.
findings.proof: Standalone has the safe model; EmbeddedCanvas lacks its guard.
findings.acceptance: Original bytes remain bit-for-bit stable.

findings.title: Preserve both versions during conflict resolution
findings.actual: Use disk and Keep mine each permanently discard one side.
findings.expected: Keep both creates a collision-free sibling first.
findings.reproduce: Create distinguishable local/disk edits and resolve each way.
findings.proof: Source audit confirms only destructive choices.
findings.seam: Workspace conflict UI + no-clobber copy API.
findings.acceptance: Both readable versions remain.

findings.title: Serialize release-channel transitions
findings.actual: Candidate, promote, and rollback mutate pointers without coordination.
findings.expected: One release lock and expected-candidate identity serialize them.
findings.reproduce: Race stage/promote and promote/rollback.
findings.proof: release_lib paths are unlocked.
findings.acceptance: Every race resolves to one valid serial history.

findings.title: Protect the loopback controller from cross-origin mutation
findings.actual: Mutating POSTs do not validate Origin, content type, or a capability.
findings.expected: Only the intended same-origin app can mutate.
findings.reproduce: POST from a foreign Origin and text/plain form.
findings.proof: Controller route audit found no gate.
findings.acceptance: Foreign requests fail without changes.

findings.title: Align the HTTP envelope limit with the document limit
findings.actual: Decoded source and escaped outer JSON share 64 MiB, so some valid documents cannot save.
findings.expected: Transport overhead gets a separate budget.
findings.reproduce: Save quote-heavy source just below 64 MiB.
findings.proof: Constants and JSON escaping reproduce it.
findings.acceptance: Below-limit decoded source saves; above-limit stays rejected.

findings.title: Make every custom color control keyboard-operable
findings.actual: Hue, opacity, and saturation/value are pointer-only with tabIndex=-1.
findings.expected: Tab reaches each control and arrows adjust it.
findings.reproduce: Edit a custom color without a pointer.
findings.proof: DOM/source audit confirmed missing handlers.
findings.acceptance: Keyboard and pointer share undo and announce values.

findings.title: Give the workspace file list correct composite-widget semantics
findings.actual: Arrow keys in the file-name input can change a row without exposing an active descendant.
findings.expected: Input editing and announced list navigation agree.
findings.reproduce: Filter, use arrows, and press Enter with a screen reader.
findings.proof: Keyboard branches and ARIA roles diverge.
findings.acceptance: The announced active row matches Enter.

findings.title: Remove the generic Inspect dead end
findings.actual: A rectangle exposes Inspect, then the panel says Select a Block.
findings.expected: Generic selections get useful content or no action.
findings.reproduce: Select a rectangle and activate Inspect.
findings.proof: A real-browser screenshot confirms the dead end.
findings.acceptance: Every visible Inspect action leads somewhere useful.

findings.title: Complete Depth Stack keyboard navigation
findings.actual: The popup lacks full menu focus, arrows, Home/End, and return focus.
findings.expected: It behaves as one keyboard menu.
findings.reproduce: Open it and traverse without a pointer.
findings.proof: Static semantic audit.
findings.acceptance: Open focuses; arrows move; Escape returns.

findings.title: Add efficient keyboard navigation to the shape grid
findings.actual: Every shape is a Tab stop and search cannot hand focus into the grid.
findings.expected: Arrow navigation traverses visible tiles.
findings.reproduce: Search Decision, press ArrowDown, navigate, insert.
findings.proof: Shape-library DOM audit.
findings.acceptance: Search-to-grid flow is predictable and announced.

findings.title: Correct command-palette tab semantics
findings.actual: Categories expose partial tab semantics.
findings.expected: Use a valid roving tablist or honest pressed buttons.
findings.reproduce: Drive categories with arrows and Tab.
findings.proof: Accessibility-tree audit.
findings.acceptance: Roles, focus, selection, and panels agree.

findings.title: Implement standard theme-radio navigation
findings.actual: Theme choices behave as many Tab stops.
findings.expected: Tab enters once and arrows apply choices.
findings.reproduce: Change theme using only Tab and arrows.
findings.proof: InterfaceSettings audit.
findings.acceptance: Selection applies; removal stays separate.

findings.title: Make the top-right capsule honest
findings.actual: The Z badge is inert and its neighbor's name does not match Comments.
findings.expected: Every visible control has a truthful action.
findings.reproduce: Click Profile placeholder.
findings.proof: Real-browser click produced no result.
findings.acceptance: No dead affordance remains.

findings.title: Add quiet first-run guidance to an empty board
findings.actual: A blank board gives no task path into Blocks, Shapes, connections, or depth.
findings.expected: A dismissible guide offers real starter actions.
findings.reproduce: Create an empty board.
findings.proof: Empty-canvas audit.
findings.acceptance: Guidance adds no records and stays reachable from Help.

findings.title: Put the production bundle in the ordinary check
findings.actual: npm run check omits a Vite production build.
findings.expected: A bundle-only failure blocks handoff.
findings.reproduce: Introduce a production-only failure and run check.
findings.proof: package.json audit.
findings.acceptance: A clean build leaves status unchanged.

findings.title: Exercise built candidate bytes before promotion
findings.actual: Promotion builds but never opens the bundle.
findings.expected: A production golden path boots, edits, saves, and reloads.
findings.reproduce: Break runtime mounting while compilation stays green.
findings.proof: Release/harness audit.
findings.acceptance: Promotion refuses a broken runtime.

findings.title: Make the browser harness fail fast on console and transport errors
findings.actual: The helper misses console.error/assert and can strand CDP promises.
findings.expected: Each error fails quickly with logs.
findings.reproduce: Emit errors, then kill Chrome mid-command.
findings.proof: Harness audit found both blind spots.
findings.acceptance: Faults fail inside a deadline with diagnostics.

findings.title: Make arbitrary worktrees reproducible
findings.actual: A generic worktree lacks dependencies; the track helper linked to an absent node_modules and wrote an unused exclude file.
findings.expected: Bootstrap resolves canonical dependencies and validates runtime.
findings.reproduce: Create a track from a dependency-less worktree.
findings.proof: This audit hit both failures.
findings.acceptance: A fresh worktree serves and checks without manual repair.
